title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/16/2026

Reason for Admission: 75 y.o. female pt admitted with aspiration pneumonia following choking episode on food at home.

Hospital Course: Pt presented with cough, fever, and dyspnea. Dx aspiration pneumonia confirmed via CXR and clinical presentation. Started on IV antibiotics. Pt remained stable on room air. Swallow evaluation performed by SLP; results indicate mild dysphagia. Pt tolerated oral intake and showed improvement in respiratory status. Afebrile and stable at time of discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Aspiration pneumonia

Discharge Medications:
- Amoxicillin 500mg BID
- Guaifenesin 600mg PRN
- Multivitamin daily

Follow-up: F/u with primary care physician in 1 week for wound check and pneumonia monitoring. See SLP for continued swallow therapy.

Electronically signed,
E. Castillo, MD
05/16/2026
explanations: Aspiration pneumonia: pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit, J69.0 (HCC 282).
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09

distractors.why: Aspiration pneumonia has its own code (HCC 282).
